text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- The Prosecutor General's Office Tuesday launched two investigations, one of solicitor Marta Tocsik on suspicion of committing a breach of law, and another of State Privatisation and Holding Co. executives for misuse of funds. @

- Solicitor Marta Tocsik confirmed she is too ill to attend Wednesday's parliamentary hearing. She made it clear that she must consider before making up her mind on repaying the over HUF 800 million she was paid and added she no longer has the entire sum.

- According to the 1997 social insurance bill submitted to Parliament, employers would have to pay a maximum of 41 percent of the employee's gross wage as social insurance contribution, slightly less than the currently paid 42.5 percent.
- The Ministry of Finance has submitted the draft of the 1997 personal income and the 1997 corporate tax laws. @
- Visiting Col. Klaus Naumann, chairman of NATO's military committee, confirmed in Budapest Tuesday that the alliance sticks by its decision on eastern expansion.

- Hungarian wages averaged HUF 30,274 net a month in the first eight months of this year, 19.5 percent up from January-August 1995, but are down by an average of 4.5 per cent in real terms, reports the Central Statistics Office.
- Duna Plaza, Budapest's newest mega shopping centre, will open on Monday.
NEPSZABADSAG @
- This daily has obtained a document which proves that the 804 million consultancy fee is not unique in Hungarian privatisation practice.
- Border guards detained two Hungarian taxi drivers near Marianosztra, who were carrying a Slovak man, and eight Lebanese nations without passports to Slovakia on their way to Germany.
NEPSZAVA
- Parliament Tuesday passed a bill on labour checks and controls and amended the act on the categorisation of the ministries. @
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Parliament voted yesterday on the amendment of the so-called Jewish compensation law.
- Parliament is expected to begin debate on ratifying the Romanian-Hungarian basic treaty in the week of October 28.
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs exuded optimism yesterday regarding Hungary's prospects for NATO membership, claiming that the expansion of the military alliance has reached a decisive stage. @
- The head of the Teachers' Union yesterday insisted on a 20 percent salary increase to offset next year's planned 18 percent rate of inflation.
- The government's liabilities undertaken in the past two years total more than HUF 2,000 billion.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The Hungarian Oil and Gas Co. (MOL) has received a $100 million loan from a syndicate.
NAPI GAZDASAG @
- The pharmaceuticals producer Richter Gedeon announced yesterday that it bought back 248,381 ordinary shares from non-stock exchange markets.
- Two huge deals in Graboplast shares helped drive volume on the Budapest Stock Exchange yesterday to an unusually high HUF 2.2 billion.
- Applications for company registration must include the tax number and the social insurance code as of October.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
